acceptMinimumLease.description: Accepts the Mac lease of a macOS sandbox (the template's `minimumLease`, `GET /v1/templates`): a whole Mac for the org for at least 24 hours, billed whatever the sandbox does. Required to create one: without it the create is `400 minimum_lease_required` and nothing is placed.

archiveSeconds.description: Sets `archiveAt` to now plus this many seconds: the sandbox is stopped then if it is running. 0 or absent: none.

deleteAfterSeconds.description: Sets `deleteAt` to now plus this many seconds (60-86400, else 400): the sandbox is then deleted, whatever its state, so it cannot outlive a client that died (`instabox run` sets it). 0 or absent: never. A server without this field ignores it.

directSecrets.description: Direct (delivery env) Secrets from this org, each as a variable and/or a home file. Real values enter the sandbox; prefer proxy Secrets for HTTPS API keys. A fork that sends none of secrets, envSecrets and directSecrets copies its source's selection.

env.description: Environment variables for the whole sandbox: every login shell exports them (exec, SSH, the terminal and what they start), from the first command on and again after each start and resume. Names match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}$`; `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, `HOME`, `HOSTNAME`, `IFS`, `LOGNAME`, `OLDPWD`, `PATH`, `PWD`, `SHELL`, `SHLVL`, `USER`, bash's readonly `BASHOPTS`, `BASH_VERSINFO`, `EUID`, `PPID`, `SHELLOPTS` and `UID`, the session's `TERM`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, the trust roots `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, and names starting `INSTABOX_` or `SSH_` are reserved (set them per exec); values have no NUL bytes; names and values at most 32 KiB together. Not on Windows templates (400). On macOS, bash and zsh login shells export them, and zsh's special parameters (`status`, `path`, `options`, `HISTSIZE`, `USERNAME`, ...) and `ZDOTDIR` are reserved too. Fixed at create: a fork takes its source's, a create from a snapshot only its own. An exec's `envs`, a Vault item and an env Secret of the same name win. Not Secrets: anything in the sandbox can read the values, and the sandbox shows only the names (`envNames`). The values are stored encrypted at rest; a site without the Secret master key refuses env (400 bad_request).

envSecrets.description: Explicit env Secret names from this org; omitted or [] selects none. No all mode; null is rejected. Real values enter the sandbox. Shorthand for directSecrets entries with env = the Secret's name; not sent together with directSecrets.

failFast.description: When no host has room for the sandbox right now, refuse the create at once with `503 no_capacity` (`retryable`; nothing is created, there is no operation and the `Idempotency-Key` is not kept) instead of answering 202 with an operation that then fails with `no_capacity`. Every other check and the rest of the create are unchanged; a host that had room can still fill up before the operation places the sandbox. The check does not ask for a host with the secret proxy, which a create with `secrets` or `envSecrets` needs: if only hosts without it have room, the create is accepted and its operation fails with `no_capacity`. A create from a snapshot that no host can start now is refused too, instead of being created stopped. A server without this field ignores it, or, if it already refuses unknown body keys, answers `400 unknown_field`.

gpu.description: GPUs for the sandbox: `TYPE` (one GPU) or `TYPE:COUNT`, such as `l4` or `l4:2`, a type of the GPU template's `gpuTypes` (`GET /v1/templates`). GPU sandboxes are for paid plans: a free org's create is `403 template_not_allowed`. The count is one of the type's `counts`: the powers of two up to its `maxPerMachine`, such as 1, 2 or 4 (a count of 3 would leave a 4-GPU host one GPU that no pair fits). An org's running sandboxes hold at most 20 GPUs in all (`403 template_limit` past it, also on a start, resume or wake; a stopped or paused sandbox holds none). The template defaults to `gpu`, and the size comes from the type: one of its `sizes`, per GPU (`l4:2` gets twice the vCPUs and memory, the same disk; `vcpus` and `memMiB` pick another of its sizes, multiplied). An unknown type, a template without GPU support or a count not in `counts` (`l4:3`) is `400 bad_request` naming the counts. With `snapshotId` of a GPU sandbox's snapshot, the snapshot's GPU type with any of its `counts` (`l4:4` from a one-GPU snapshot), sized from that count; another type is `400 bad_request`, and absent `gpu` gets the snapshot's own count (a snapshot of a 3-GPU sandbox, from before the rule, is `400 bad_request` until `gpu` names one of the counts). GPUs are billed per GPU-hour while the sandbox runs, on top of its vCPUs and memory. Absent: no GPU (from a snapshot: the snapshot's GPU).

guestUser.description: The sandbox's Linux user (`Machine.guestUser`), so `ssh <sandbox>` over your own network (Tailscale) logs in as the same name as on your computer. Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters; reserved names (`root`, `instabox`, the Debian base system's users and groups such as `sudo`, `systemd-*`) are refused with `400 invalid_guest_user`. Clients send the local username normalized (`DOMAIN\alice` and `alice@corp.example` become `alice`, lowercase, spaces become `_`) and nothing when that is not a valid name. Absent: `user`; with `snapshotId`, the snapshot's user. Ignored (the sandbox gets `dev`) for templates without the `guest-user` capability. Fixed at create.

imageId.description: Deprecated: `snapshotId` under its old name (both: they must be equal). The reply carries a `Deprecation` header.

memMiB.description: Like vcpus: the memory (MiB) of one of your sizes, such as 8192 with vcpus 4; 0 or a negative is `400 bad_request`.

model.description: The Mac model of a macOS template with `models`, by its `name`: the sandbox runs on that model's Macs, at one of that model's sizes. Absent: the template's `pool`, or its first open model when that pool's model is `closed`. With `snapshotId`: the model to run the snapshot on, at that model's sizes; absent, the snapshot's own `model` unless it is closed.

name.description: 1-63 lowercase letters, digits or `-`, starting with a letter or digit; unique among the org's sandboxes. Absent or empty: `box-` and 8 random hex digits (the operation's `machineId` and the sandbox carry it).

networkPolicy.description: Limits where the sandbox may connect to, from its first boot. Absent: no limit. A sandbox from a snapshot takes only its own. Linux sandboxes only: a GPU, macOS or Windows sandbox is refused (400). While no host can apply a policy the create is refused (`503 host_unavailable`) and nothing is created. Only where the server offers network policies: elsewhere this field is unknown (`400 unknown_field`).

orgId.description: The org the sandbox counts against and is shared with (`GET /v1/orgs`); you must be a member. Absent: your personal org, or with `snapshotId` the snapshot's org (a sandbox from a snapshot lives in the snapshot's org; another is `400 bad_request`). Secret selections always resolve within this org. The org's sandbox limit and, on the free tier, its monthly included usage apply (`429 quota_exceeded`, `402 credit_exhausted`).

persistentDiskGiB.description: Storage (`/data`) size in GiB. The disks come with the size: storage gets the size's (20 GiB on api.instabox.sh), or a snapshot's storage size when that is larger. Absent or exactly that size: accepted; any other is `400 spec_not_allowed` whose message names the size's storage next to what was asked; 0 or a negative is `400 bad_request`. To get more storage, grow it later with `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}`: a running sandbox's storage grows live, and a shrink applies while it is stopped, at its next boot. The SDKs' `diskGiB` (TypeScript) and `persistent_disk_gib` (Python) are this field; `diskGiB` in a REST body is `400 unknown_field`.

pool.description: Admins only: the host pool to place the sandbox in and no other (docs/hybrid-pools.md), "default" included. With snapshotId it must be the snapshot's pool. Absent: the user's pool assignment, else the server's placement.createPools.

queue.description: Wait for a GPU instead of failing with `no_capacity` (a create with `gpu`, or from a GPU snapshot; not with `failFast`, else `400 bad_request`). The answer is the usual 202 operation. When a GPU of the type is free the sandbox is placed as without `queue`; when none is, or the type already has requests waiting, the operation ends `succeeded` with the sandbox `stopped` and `Machine.queue` set (its place in line and `expiresAt`). The dispatcher starts it when a GPU frees up, workspaces holding fewer GPUs first, then the oldest request. If none frees up by `expiresAt`, a create from a template is deleted (it never had data) and one from a snapshot stays `stopped` with its disks. An org has at most a few live entries (`429 queue_limit`). A server without the GPU queue, or with it off, refuses the field with `400 unknown_field`, as for any field it does not have. A macOS create or start (with `acceptMinimumLease`) waits for a Mac of its model the same way where `Me.macQueue` is true: oldest request first, one live entry per workspace and model (`429 queue_limit`). A Mac that frees up is reserved for the first in line (`Machine.queue.state` `offered`) and a start of the sandbox takes it, or `autoLease` starts it at once.

rootDiskGiB.description: System files size in GiB. Like persistentDiskGiB: system files get the template's size (or the snapshot's); naming any other is `400 spec_not_allowed` (the message names the size's root disk), 0 or a negative `400 bad_request`; grow it later with `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}`.

secrets.description: Proxy Secrets from this org. All includes current and future proxy Secrets; [] selects none. Omit both secrets and envSecrets to retain only existing Vault delivery. When envSecrets alone is supplied, proxy selection defaults to all; directSecrets alone selects no proxy Secrets. Null is rejected.

snapshotId.description: Create from this snapshot of yours: its system files and storage (empty storage for a system-files-only snapshot).

templateId.description: The template to create from (`GET /v1/templates`, one with `creatable` true), optionally with a version as `id@version` (e.g. `agent-browser@2026-10-15.4`, the same as `templateVersion`). Absent (and no `snapshotId` or `templateVersion`): agent-browser. An unknown or retired one is refused with `400 bad_request` whose message lists the templates your plan can create from. The free plan creates from agent-browser, android, omarchy or ci only; another template is refused with `403 template_not_allowed`. A create from a snapshot is not limited.

templateVersion.description: Default: the version `GET /v1/templates` marks `latest`. `templateId` may name it instead, as `id@version` (e.g. `agent-browser@2026-10-15.4`); both at once must agree. A version the template does not have is `400 bad_request` whose message lists its versions, newest first, the `latest` (or `default`) one tagged.

vault.description: False disables legacy Vault delivery. Org Secret selections are independent.

vcpus.description: Absent: the default size (4 vCPUs, 8 GiB memory; `limits.machineSpec`). From a snapshot with `sizeLocked` (not of a GPU sandbox): the vCPUs and memory of the sandbox it was saved from (the snapshot's `defaultSpec`), absent or named; any other is `400 spec_not_allowed` stating the snapshot's size, and that size is `403 spec_not_allowed` while the org's plan does not offer it (upgrade the plan). A snapshot without `sizeLocked` (saved before this rule) takes any size below. Else one of the org's sizes (`GET /v1/orgs` `allowedSpecs`: the default, its plan's others and any size an admin granted the org; on api.instabox.sh free 4/8192 only, Pro 2/4096, 4/8192, 8/16384, Builder 2/4096 up to 16/32768, Team and Enterprise 2/4096 up to 32/65536), or, from a template with a `pool` (macOS, Windows), its `defaultSpec` or one of its `sizes`, whatever the plan; name memMiB too when two of them have this many vCPUs. Anything else is refused with `400 spec_not_allowed`; 0 or a negative (no size) with `400 bad_request`.

id.description: Sandbox ID (`m_` + 26 lowercase base32 characters) or the sandbox's name (unique among your sandboxes; names never contain `_`, so the two never collide). Older servers take only the ID and answer `404` for a name.

argv.description: The program and its arguments, run with no shell: each element reaches the program exactly as sent (no expansion of `$`, `*` or `~`, no word splitting, quotes or redirections; `""` is an empty argument). `argv[0]` must not be empty and is looked up on the login profile's `PATH`; the login profile, `envs` and `cwd` apply as for `cmd`. A program that is not found exits 127, one that cannot run 126. At most 64 KiB counting each element's length plus one, no NUL bytes. The command sent to the sandbox (`envs`, `cwd` and `argv`, quoted for the shell: about 9 bytes per element plus its text) must also stay under 128 KiB, so many short elements can be `400 bad_request` below the 64 KiB cap; send bulk data on `stdin`. Set this or `cmd`.

cmd.description: Shell command, run with `bash -lc`. At most 64 KiB, no NUL bytes. Set this or `argv`; an empty `cmd` is no `cmd`.

envs.description: Environment variables exported before the command (after the login profile). Names match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`.

historyCommand.description: How the command appears in the sandbox's history instead of `cmd` or `argv`, for a wrapper that runs something else (the CLI's `exec --background`). Cut at 4096 bytes like them; no NUL bytes.

noHistory.description: Leave the command out of the sandbox's history (`GET /v1/machines/{id}/history`): for a client's own housekeeping commands, such as the CLI's job polls. Does not go with `historyCommand`.

secretEnvs.description: Direct (delivery env) Secrets of the sandbox's org exported for this command only: variable name -> Secret name. Resolved at exec time, never stored or written into the sandbox; each use is audited by name. A name may not also be in `envs`; reserved variables are refused. A proxy or missing Secret is 400. Only where `GET /v1/me` has `directSecretRefs`; elsewhere 400 (a control host from before secretEnvs would run the command without them).

stdin.description: Text fed to the command, then EOF. It is a JSON string, so the command reads its UTF-8 bytes: NUL, CR and LF arrive unchanged (escaped as `\u0000`, `\r`, `\n`). At most 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) of UTF-8, counted in bytes, not characters (`é` is 2): more is `400 bad_request` `stdin is longer than 1048576 bytes`. The schema sets no `maxLength` here, because `maxLength` counts characters. JSON cannot carry bytes that are not UTF-8; any in the request body reach the command as U+FFFD (`ef bf bd`), with no error. For binary input, send it base64-encoded and decode it in the command (`base64 -d | ...`; up to 768 KiB of binary fits), or write the file first with `PUT /v1/machines/{id}/files` and redirect it in (`cmd < file`). The CLI's `exec --stdin` does that upload itself for input past 1 MiB or not UTF-8, up to 5 GiB.

queue.description: For a stopped GPU sandbox: wait for a GPU instead of failing with `no_capacity`, as `CreateMachineRequest.queue`. On a sandbox without GPUs it is `400 bad_request`; on a server without the GPU queue, `400 unknown_field`. A stopped macOS sandbox waits for a Mac the same way, as `CreateMachineRequest.queue`.

rescue.description: Boot a stopped sandbox without running its data-init.d hooks (`/usr/local/lib/instabox/data-init.d`, the template's and your own), so a hook that blocks the boot can be fixed from inside. Everything else of the boot runs; the next start runs the hooks again. A running sandbox is `409 operation_conflict` (stop it first), and so is a paused one, which resumes without booting (resume it, then stop it), and so is joining an active start that is not a rescue. A sandbox whose host runs a node-agent without rescue starts fails the operation (`host_unavailable`) and stays stopped.

vault.description: False disables legacy Vault delivery without changing org Secret selections.

vcpus.description: Start a stopped paid sandbox at another of the workspace's `allowedSpecs`, as `PATCH` `vcpus`/`memMiB` then `start` would: with `memMiB`, one of them (alone: the one size with that many vCPUs). Absent: its current size. The size is stored before the start and the boot asks for it; read it from the sandbox's `spec` (the start Operation carries no request body). Its current size changes nothing; a running sandbox at another size is `409 operation_conflict` (stop it first), and so is a paused one (resume it, then stop it), as is a sandbox whose start is already active (naming it: only the same size, or none, joins that start); another size, or the free sandbox, is `400 spec_not_allowed`; 0 or a negative is `400 bad_request`.

A refused value leaves the setting unchanged; the reply shows the effective value. API keys follow the owner's policy. Separately, with manual lifecycle (`GET /v1/me`) or an admin sign-in session: 120-86400, or 0 (off). Absent: unchanged.

A refusal leaves the earlier policy in force. `409 operation_conflict` while the sandbox has an operation in progress. Only where the server offers network policies: elsewhere this field is unknown (`400 unknown_field`).

persistentDiskGiB.description: New disk (`/data`) size in GiB, 1-1024, up to the plan's `maxDiskGiB`; 0 or absent: unchanged. Grow: a running box grows online (no restart, processes keep running); if it can't (rare: the box is unreachable or its host is older), `409 grow_needs_stop` (stop it and send the size again); a stopped box grows at its next start. Shrink: only while stopped (else `409 operation_conflict`), and only when the used data plus 10% (at least 1 GiB) fits; else `409 disk_too_small`, with the smallest size that fits in the message, and the box unchanged. Past 1024 is `400 bad_request`, and so is growing on a template without the `root-grow` capability (a shrink needs none); a free box's disk is fixed (`400 spec_not_allowed`, running or stopped). Running is `409 operation_conflict` (stop it first), and so is paused (resume it, then stop it); another size, or the free sandbox, is `400 spec_not_allowed`.

The plan decides, and a value is honoured or refused, never silently replaced: a paid sandbox takes 300-1800 (5 to 30 minutes) in whole minutes, as sent, and 0 (off) where the plan allows always on (else `403 spec_not_allowed`); below 300 (1-299), above 1800, negative or not a multiple of 60 is `400 bad_request`. capabilities.description: `mosh`: mosh works (a session that runs `mosh-server new` gets a relay UDP port in its `MOSH CONNECT` line).

moshHost.description: Optional separate Mosh gateway host; defaults to host when absent.

moshPort.description: SSH port for Mosh session bootstrap; defaults to port when absent. The UDP relay port is negotiated during bootstrap.

actions.description: The computer-use MCP's last tool calls (at most 20, oldest first), as its proxy logged them.

agentPausable.description: The sandbox's computer-use MCP honors the control (its wrapper runs the server through the proxy). False on a sandbox made before the proxy existed: a takeover would not pause its agent, so clients should offer watching only.

controlError.description: The control file in the sandbox could not be written (its runtime directory is missing or not writable): takeover and handback cannot take effect. The reason, from the sandbox.

controller.description: Who drives the desktop: `agent` (the default; viewers watch) or `human` (a viewer took over, and the computer-use MCP refuses input until they hand back or 30 s pass without a call from them).

failed.description: The last install failed; log holds its last lines.

hint.description: Only on a `start` that started nothing because the desktop is not installed (`start` never installs), is still installing, or failed to install: what to send next. Absent otherwise.

kind.description: The desktop the sandbox has. `vm` (a Windows or Mac sandbox): its VM's own screen, always running and controlled by every viewer (`controller` `human`, `yours`); `install`, `start`, `takeover` and `handback` change nothing. `x11` (absent from servers before this field): Xvnc and Xfce, installed on first use, driven by the computer-use MCP. `wayland` (the omarchy template): a compositor that starts at boot and is in the image: `install` changes nothing, `start` only brings the session and its VNC server up and sizes the display, and there is no computer-use MCP (`agentPausable` is false); watch and use it through VNC.

os.description: Only on `kind` `vm`: the guest OS. Clients map keys by it: on `macos`, a Mac's Command is the guest's Command (keysym Alt_L) and Option its Option (Meta_L).

running.description: The VNC server answers: GET /v1/machines/{id}/vnc connects.

yours.description: The caller (its sign-in session or API key) is the viewer in control. Absent when false.

args.description: Its arguments, strings shortened to 80 characters.

refused.description: Refused because a human controlled the desktop; it never reached the tool.

tool.description: The MCP tool called (click, type_text, get_app_state, ...).

url.description: The dashboard's full-screen viewer, `<dashboard>/desktop/{id}#token=...`; open it or embed it in an iframe.

DirectSecret.description: A reference to a direct (delivery env) Secret: its real value as the variable `env` (exported by login shells), as a file at `file` (home-relative; the value stays on tmpfs at /run/instabox/secrets/files and the home path is a symlink to it), or both. Names and paths only; values are never returned.

env.description: Not reserved (PATH, HOME, BASH_ENV, IFS, CA variables, ...) and no INSTABOX_ or SSH_ prefix.

file.description: Clean path relative to the home directory, without .. components.

message.description: What is full and how to free or add space (delete files, `instabox resize <box> --disk N` for /data: a running sandbox's disk grows live).

mount.description: The fullest filesystem (empty when it could not be read after a command ran out of space).

noSpace.description: The command failed with No space left on device (or Disk quota exceeded).

at.description: When it happened, for a stop the platform found (a sandbox's `lastError` with code `host_oom`, `vmm_crashed` or `guest_reboot_loop`; `hint` says what to do). The next successful start clears the error. Absent otherwise and from older servers.

code.description: Machine-readable code. HTTP status per code is fixed.

docs.description: A URL documenting the error (credential errors). Absent otherwise.

docs_url.description: The code's entry on the errors page, on every error response: https://instabox.sh/docs/errors#<code> with underscores as dashes (e.g. #credit-exhausted): its HTTP status, whether to retry and what to do. Snake case, unlike the other fields. Absent from a failed operation's `error` and from older servers.

hint.description: The next step that fixes the error (credential errors, a start quota's refusal). Absent otherwise.

reason.description: The same as `code` for credential errors (401 `missing_key`, `malformed_key`, `invalid_key`, `expired_key`, `revoked_key`, `session_expired`; 403 `missing_scope`). For 409 `machine_cooldown`, the automatic abuse check whose pause locks the sandbox: `abuse_egress_blocklist` (it tried to connect to a blocked destination on the egress blocklist, not a DNS lookup), `abuse_network_flows` (scanning or attack traffic), `abuse_cpu` (mining); absent for a max-run cooldown. For a retryable 409 `fork_unavailable`, why the source's host cannot take the fork: `source_host_unavailable` (it takes no new sandboxes) or `source_host_full` (no room now). For a 409 `fork_unavailable` that is not retryable, `source_not_local` when the source is stopped and its host no longer keeps a local copy of it. For a card top-up's 402 `payment_failed`: `card_declined`, or `authentication_required` (the bank asks to confirm the payment; pay with `newCard`). For a create's 429 `rate_limited`: `creates_per_day` when it is the workspace's plan's sandbox creates a day, which resets at 00:00 UTC; `starts_per_day`, `starts_per_hour` or `starts_per_minute` when it is the workspace's start quota in the last 24 hours, hour or minute (Retry-After: when enough creates leave the window, an hour at most; `hint` the next step); absent for its starts a minute. Absent on other errors and from older servers.

requiredScopes.description: For `missing_scope`, the scopes the route accepts; the key needs one of them.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Seconds to wait before trying again: a retryable `no_capacity` (60, as a 503 or on a failed operation's `error`), `rate_limited`, `machine_cooldown` and agent sign-up `quota_exceeded`. An error response also sends it as the `Retry-After` header; a failed operation's `error` has only this field. Absent otherwise and from older servers.

retryable.description: True if the same request may succeed later.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next (older) page; absent on the last page.

ExecHistoryEntry.description: One command of a sandbox's history: an exec request that reached the sandbox, whoever sent it, as the server recorded it. `stdout` and `stderr` are set only by `GET /v1/machines/{id}/history/{execId}`.

command.description: The request's `cmd`, its `argv` quoted for a shell, or its `historyCommand`; cut at 4096 bytes.

outputTruncated.description: The stored output is cut: the history keeps the first 64 KiB of each stream.

signal.description: The signal that killed the command, as the sandbox named it (absent otherwise).

status.description: How the command ended: `exited` (exit code reported; `signal` set if a signal killed it), `timed_out` (killed after `timeoutSeconds`), `lost` (the connection to the sandbox ended before the exit status; it may have run), `cancelled` (the client closed the request; the command was killed) or `unreachable` (the sandbox could not be reached; nothing ran).

streamed.description: The client streamed the output (`Accept: text/event-stream`).

truncated.description: The exec's result had its output cut at 1 MiB per stream (never for a streamed exec).

diskWarning.description: Set when the command failed with No space left on device (read again right after it), or a filesystem was at least 90% full when last read (read in the background after an exec or metrics call, at most once a minute).

exitCode.description: Exit status; 128+N if killed by standard signal N, otherwise 255 with `signal` set; 124 if timed out.

invalidUtf8.description: stdout or stderr had bytes that are not UTF-8 (binary output), replaced with U+FFFD, so the output is not what the command wrote. Absent when false; also set on a streamed exec's exit event.

oomKill.description: The OOM kill behind `oomKilled` (the newest, when several).

Checked only for exit code 137, a signal, or stderr saying a process was killed. False when none was seen, the exec's session scope could not be read, or the sandbox's host or guest agent cannot report kills; a kill whose kernel log record was lost is still true when the session scope's oom_kill count shows it (`oomKill` absent). Absent from older servers. Also set on a streamed exec's exit event.

signal.description: The signal that killed the command, as the sandbox named it (absent otherwise).

timedOut.description: The command ran past `timeoutSeconds` and was killed.

truncated.description: stdout or stderr was longer than 1 MiB and was cut.

sources.description: The sandboxes and snapshots the caller may export, each with its newest export that has not expired.

machineName.description: The sandbox's name; absent once it is deleted.
